The Discount Rate Is the Price of Waiting, and It Can Reorder Projects

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-convention: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-convention: npf.npv does not discount values[0]; end-of-period convention: 'Shifting every flow one year later divides the whole NPV by 1.07.' At 8%, 96.3 x 1.08 = 104.0.
recorded.prompt:q-irr: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-irr: 'IRR does not rank projects... Rank by NPV at the chosen rate; use IRR, if at all, as a description.'
recorded.prompt:q-factor: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-factor: Discount factor table: 20 years at 7% = 0.2584; P = F/(1+r)^n, so 2000 x 0.2584 = about 517.

recorded.prompt:q-convention:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-convention:a: 'Mixing them is [wrong]... the second is understated' - the two conventions give different NPVs on the same flows and rate.
recorded.prompt:q-convention:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-convention:c: npf.npv uses t=0 for the first value, so it discounts one year less than the end-of-period convention, not more ('values[0] is divided by (1+r)^0 = 1').
recorded.prompt:q-convention:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-convention:d: 'Shifting every flow one year later divides the whole NPV by 1.07' - every amount shifts, not only the first.
recorded.prompt:q-irr:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-irr:a: 'IRR measures how fast a project returns money, not how much value it adds'; rank by NPV.
recorded.prompt:q-irr:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-irr:b: IRR is the rate at which its own NPV is zero; it does not measure value 'at the organization's own cost of money'.
recorded.prompt:q-irr:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-irr:c: 'Rank by NPV at the chosen rate' - the page's rule gives a decision even when IRR disagrees.
recorded.prompt:q-factor:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-factor:b: Table gives 0.2584 at 20 years, 7%; discounting shrinks, not adds. (833 matches no 7% row.)
recorded.prompt:q-factor:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-factor:c: 'A Dollar Later Is Worth Less Than a Dollar Now'; only a payment now (n = 0) is undiscounted.
recorded.prompt:q-factor:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-factor:d: 'at 7%, a dollar ten years out is worth about 51 cents' - halving is ten years; twenty years gives 0.2584.
